title: 3D Viewport Grid in Editor is VERY Performance Heavy when using D3D12 instead of Vulkan
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproduceable in: v4.6.2.stable.steam [71f334935]

### System information

Windows 11 - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 32 GB RAM

### Issue description

After performing a number of tests it appears that there are two performance issues with the grid shown in 3D viewports in the Godot Editor:

1. The grid appears to be being rendered well beyond its visible range, requiring more GPU power to render than it should, especially when the horizon is visible. While this normally wouldn't be that big a deal, it compounds the second issue below.
2.  When the rendering driver is set to "d3d12" instead of "Vulkan", the amount of GPU power needed to render the grid in the 3D viewport is about 5x greater than usual. With my GTX1070 card this a difference between requiring 6% total power with Vulkan and 30% total power with D3D12.

The only catch is that I am not sure if this is a "bug" or not, as video cards are optimized for polygons, not lines. Nevertheless, I wanted to bring this up just in case this performance discrepancy is not normal.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new project on Windows with a 3D scene. Ensure the Windows renderer in the Project Settings is set to "d3d12".
2. Go into the "Perspective" menu in the 3D viewport and turn on "View Frame Time".
3. Make note of how much GPU time is being consumed.
4. Go back into the "Perspective" menu and turn off "View Grid". The amount of GPU time being consumed should plummet.
5. While the grid is visible, you can also experiment with how much GPU time is being used to render non-visible portions of the grid by making sure the horizon is visible, go to the "View -> Settings..." menu for the viewport, and adjust the "View Z-Far" value to smaller numbers.
